_README: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for stop-model work across sessions and accounts. Every session reads this first and updates it before ending. Do NOT restate this status in prose anywhere else -- a second copy is how drift starts. `python3 scripts/state.py` renders it as a table AND verifies every `verify` probe below against the real code, failing loudly when a claim and the codebase disagree.
audit_rule: NOTHING counts as done until an adversarial round comes back clean. audit_rounds counts rounds RUN; audit_clean is true only when a round found nothing. A phase with status=shipped and audit_clean=false is NOT finished. This applies to `already_shipped` entries identically -- being written in that list means the CODE is done, never that the WORK is.

phases.name: Piece 4 -- per-position premium stop
phases.note: Built and green. TWO adversarial rounds run, NEITHER clean. Round 1 found 8 defects (all fixed). Round 2 found 8 more in this phase alone, all fixed: the frontend PREMIUM_STOP copied only one of the backend's two guards, so a failed quote (currentPrice coerced to 0) fired a Critical toast for EVERY position on every 30s cycle with no backend alert behind it -- a regression the pnlPct test it replaced did not have; the card displayed one premium stop and posted another, twice over (the reset re-seeds the field without telling the parent cache, and mergePlan swaps `exit` under an overridden card without changing `contract` so nothing re-runs -- the second reproduced the 78% stop that round 1 was supposed to have killed); a dollar stop at or beyond the entry fell back silently and also discarded a valid client-sent fraction; the drawer cleared the override on any entry >= 100 and persisted every keystroke, so typing '45' armed a 4% stop; the server-derived fraction was dropped from the create response, leaving the two engines disagreeing until the next sync; a dead schema field; and two tests that asserted plumbing while claiming to cover behaviour -- the router derivation and the PATCH write had NO test, and now go through the endpoint. NOT YET CLEAN -- round 3 pending. || ROUND 3 (combined, all three items at once) found 14 more and every one was fixed; audit_clean stays FALSE until a round comes back clean. The CRITICAL was the same display-vs-posted split round 2 thought it had closed, reached by REVERSING the order of the two events: an unrelated edit BEFORE a mergePlan caches the old seed, the re-seed effect then moves the field without telling the parent, and premiumStopDollarToSend compared the stale cache against the NEW seed and let it through -- card showing $0.80 while $1.50 was posted. Root cause was inferring touched-ness by comparing values; it is now TRACKED and threaded to the page via onEditsChange's meta.touched.premiumStop, which also fixes the mirror defect (a user who typed the seed's own value back had the choice discarded). Also: the offline-retry path in syncFromBackend dropped the server-derived premiumStopPct, leaving the two engines disagreeing; the auto-trader test asserted the resolver directly and never called fire() or _check_daily_loss, so BOTH call sites could be reverted with 75 tests still green (replaced with two that drive the service and fail on that mutation); entryPrice had no gt=0 so a non-positive entry silently dropped the user's dollar stop unlogged; the drawer rewrote a stored stop on a bare focus-and-blur (0.4843 rendered '48' and committed 0.48) and could not represent sub-1% or >=99.5% fractions at all; and the persisted store gained two fields with no version bump (now v3). ROUND 5 (11 findings, all fixed): the badge percentage came from the printed pair while the badge's COLOUR and tooltip (`status`) still came from full precision, so at a 0.70 pass line $1.77 away x 0.789 on a $2.00 premium printed '70% OF PREMIUM' in PASS green above an equation that hand-checks to exactly 70% (~0.18% of ordinary inputs) -- the verdict now comes from the same printed pair, via one shared printedFrom(); a sub-cent premium produced a card of four contradictory zeroes ('0%' badge, total-loss tooltip, '$0 of $0 premium') and now returns null into the existing N/A path; PremiumStopEditor's two REVERT paths returned without clearing dirtyRef, so typing 100, blurring, then merely clicking in and out PATCHed a live stop nobody touched -- round 4's defect re-entered through the rejected-edit path; lastStoredRef's 'never while the user is mid-edit' was asserted but not implemented (a 30s sync overwrote typing); FastAPI's `detail` is a LIST for a validation 422 and all four parse sites cast it to string, so entryPrice's new gt=0 bound could crash the whole Portfolio page via detail.split(); the card's premium-stop field was min=0.01 with no max, so typing 0 -- the natural way to say 'no override' -- clamped to $0.01 and pinned a 0.19% stop (Critical alert on the first cent of adverse move, and a ~3000x cut to the auto-trader's daily-loss denominator), now bounded to 10-99% of the mid to match the global's own ge=0.10 bound; the router's live-quote guard tested the RAW quote and rounded after, so a $0.004 quote stored entry_price 0.0, which alert_generator's `entry_price > 0` gate makes permanently unable to raise a stop alert; the Alerts page rendered the resolved stop through Math.round, reprinting the exact 0%/100% lossiness premiumStop.ts documents as fixed; and AutoTradeArm's doc comment claimed arming and sending 'cannot arm a position at two different stops' when they share only the DOLLAR by design. ROUND 6 (11 findings; 10 fixed, 1 escalated to Kenneth): round 5's own 10-99%-of-mid bounds RE-OPENED the stray-click defect rounds 4 and 5 closed -- EditableKV.save clamps BEFORE its no-op guard, so when the SEED sits outside the bounds the clamp alone makes next !== value and a bare focus-and-blur reports a deliberate edit; the seed is round(mid x global, 2) and the global is allowed up to 1.0, at which point 1951 of 2000 mids from $0.01-$20.00 seed above the max. Now guarded on the PRE-CLAMP draft, with a test verified to fail without it. Also: the badge dropped the schematic's verdict word (StatusBadge renders `label ?? STATUS_LABEL`, so a supplied label REPLACES it), leaving colour as the only thing separating two badges that both print '70% of premium' with opposite verdicts -- the word is back and leads the badge, matching the schematic; the sub-cent guard tested the ROUNDED premium and (0.005).toFixed(2) rounds UP to 0.01, so it never rejected the case it was written for (now on the raw premium, and its test no longer claims 0.005 is 'exactly one cent'); the drawer's 'Fires at premium $X' rounded half-up while both engines compare at full precision, advertising a price that fires nothing (now floored); the two engines wrote position_alert_history reference_value at two precisions; two assertions compared literals to literals and could not fail; and three comments asserted live failure paths that the render gate, the schema bound and market.py respectively foreclose. || ROUNDS 7 AND 8 were recorded only in their commit messages (c39eb7e5, 05627fa1) and never here, under a green state.py -- a presence probe cannot see a missing narrative. Round 7: 17 findings, 15 fixed, 1 rejected on arithmetic, 1 recorded; the trade-affecting ones were the Monte Carlo and its staleness guard still falling back to data.exit.invalidation while the position is stopped at overlay.invalidation, the Invalidation field becoming PortfolioPosition.stop with no bound or directional check, roundCents's Number.EPSILON nudge being arithmetically inert above ~$2 (2999 of 4,995,000 pairs mis-rounded, moving the VERDICT), handleEditsChange early-returning on a null contract key so a typed limit was displayed and dropped, and the three edit caches surviving a setScanResult. Round 8: 13 findings, 11 fixed, 1 rejected after building it, 1 partly deferred; the CRITICAL was the Entry limit reaching the broker unbounded, and finding 4 was a REGRESSION from round 7's own fix (<input type='number'> sanitizes any half-typed literal to '', which round 7 had made mean 'revert to inheriting'). || ROUND 9 (17 findings: 1 CRITICAL, 4 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM-HIGH, 5 MEDIUM, 1 LOW-MEDIUM, 5 LOW) -- all 17 fixed, and audit_clean STAYS FALSE until a round comes back clean. The CRITICAL was reached through the one path nobody had looked at, the SERVER: portfolio.py re-anchors `stop` by (live - scanStockPrice) so a plan level still sits the right distance from the underlying, and this branch made that field a price the USER TYPES -- round 8 even bounded it against the live quote -- so $180 typed on a $200 stock scanned at $145 stored $235, ABOVE spot, raising a Critical STOP_REACHED with Gmail and Telegram behind it on the first backend scan. A new `stopIsUserSet` flag exempts only `stop`. Also: the optimistic row adopted the server's premiumStopPct while keeping the CLIENT's entryPrice, so the two engines compared `price <= entry * (1 - pct)` against different entries (a $3.12 stop filled at $4.00 became $4.06 locally) -- which is also why round 7's rejection of the entry-limit finding did not cover it: that identity holds only when ONE entry is used for both derivation and threshold; at the EXACT pass line the badge said PASS above an equation hand-checking to CAUTION, because round 5 moved the verdict onto the printed pair and then compared it with a float quotient (0.16/0.20 is 0.7999999999999999), now cross-multiplied in integer cents; a half-typed decimal COMMITTED a truncation (parseFloat('2.') is 2, Number('48.') is 48), so round 8 had traded 'reverts to a value the user didn't choose' for 'commits a value the user didn't choose' and only the second reaches a broker; AutoTradeArm still anchored entry_premium on the scan-time mid, mis-sizing the backend daily-loss gate by 2.4x on a stale scanResult; the backend never got round 8's bounds at all (limit_price now gt=0 on all three order schemas, and a user-set stop on the wrong side of the live underlying is now a 422); the 'premium stop could not be applied' notice covered 2 of 4 create paths and the two that had it overwrote each other's note; the Barrier Race simulated an UNTOUCHED seed against the fresh premium and labelled it 'from the editable field above'; and the reject-don't-clamp policy gave no feedback at all, which a test now pins. Four test/doc defects: the spec-8 two-send-path test was a TAUTOLOGY (one pure function called twice with one argument, the results compared to each other) in the block whose header calls it 'the mandated test that shipped missing' -- replaced with a page-level test driving Place Limit and a basket submit, verified to fail when only the basket path is reverted; round 6's Math.floor on the drawer preview was unpinned (mutating it to Math.round left all 69 tests green); two doc blocks on the bounds were ORPHANED and both asserted the opposite of their code; and AGENTS.md kept the overstated state.py claim that round 7 corrected in CLAUDE.md.

already_shipped.name: Stop-cost notation rework
already_shipped.note: Frontend copy only, no logic change. Round 1 fixed the headline's three independently-rounded figures. ROUND 2 found the equation STILL did not reconcile, in both directions, because `r.capped` is decided at full precision while the line prints a 3dp delta: capped with the product below the premium printed '(uncapped $38.55)' beside '$38.59 of $38.59' -- an uncapped figure BELOW the capped one, impossible by construction; uncapped with the product above printed '= $52.48 of $52.48' where the printed factors give $52.52, with no tail, above a headline claiming '$0 left' for a stop the code did not classify as a total loss. Round 1's own range test could not have caught either: it skipped every capped row and re-implemented the clamp as the expected value. Both now decided on the printed product. Round 2 also found the badge's percentage still came from full precision while the headline came from the printed pair ('100% OF PREMIUM' beside '$8 left'), and that 'of the $X you paid' names a scan-time mid that the editable Limit and the contracts-scaled CaR both contradict. THIRD TIME THIS ITEM HAS SHIPPED A NON-RECONCILING FIGURE. NOT YET CLEAN. || ROUND 3 (combined, all three items at once) found 14 more and every one was fixed; audit_clean stays FALSE until a round comes back clean. The badge TOOLTIP was the last consumer of full-precision `capped` while the label and headline beside it came from printedShare, so with ordinary 4dp deltas it called a contract a total loss above '99% OF PREMIUM' and '$1 left' ($55.92 x 0.1622 on a $9.07 premium). Now branches on stopLossIsTotalOnPrintedFigures and is pinned by a sweep that fails on the mutation. Separately, the printed product used toFixed(2), which breaks an exact half-cent on the BINARY value: 8.01 x 0.500 = 4.005 printed $4.00 where a hand-check gives $4.01 -- and that is this rework's OWN documented worked example, with three tests pinning the artefact. Rounding is now explicit half-up (roundCents) and the range sweep re-derives the rule independently rather than importing it. ROUND 5: the badge's percentage and its COLOUR were decided at two different precisions (see phase D note) -- fixed at the root so one printed pair drives the verdict, the percentage, the headline and the tooltip. Sub-cent premiums no longer render at all. AND the badge now carries the dollars left, per share, per decision BADGE-SPEC-2026-09-05. ROUND 6: the badge now LEADS WITH THE VERDICT WORD, as the schematic always had it -- round 5's label replaced it, and without it two cards printing the same rounded percentage on opposite sides of the pass line were distinguishable only by colour. The round-5 comment claiming the ambiguity was eliminated is corrected: the verdict agrees with the printed EQUATION always, but the whole-percent figure is rounded and the verdict is not, so the word is what separates them.

already_shipped.name: Schematic removals -- Invalidation readout + Projected R/R
already_shipped.note: Both approved by Kenneth. (1) The Final Recommendation's standalone invalidation probability -- its no-race fallback -- is gone; the Monte Carlo card's own copy had already moved to the Barrier Race. firstPassage.invalidation and data.exit.invalidation are untouched, so the send gate still fires. (2) The Projected R/R (+8%) readout is gone from the Final Recommendation's Ladder-DEFAULT branch -- the copy that survived its removal from the Ladder section itself, and the one seen first since it is the card's opening state. overlay.premiumStop stays. KNOCK-ON: computeEditedRR, isDirty and the `dirty` memo were deleted as dead, which removes the card-level 'edited' flag (see open question). UNAUDITED. ROUND 1 confirmed every stated invariant of the removals holds, and found two comment defects: one promised a stop the branch does not print, one implied a freshness guarantee scoped only to the race. Both corrected.  ROUND 2 re-checked the orphan sweep independently and confirmed it: isDirty/computeEditedRR had no other callers, data.rrRatio/rrModel are still consumed by the context rail, firstPassage.invalidation still feeds BarrierRaceCard, data.exit.invalidation still hard-blocks the send, and the per-target 'edited' badge survives. Two more comment defects found and fixed: an orphaned JSDoc (the new stopCostShown prop was inserted between `invalidation`'s doc block and `invalidation`, so tooling attributed the standalone-invalidation description to it), and the section header still promising the Ladder-default branch prints 'T1/T2/T3 + R:R' when the R:R is exactly what was removed. NOT YET CLEAN. || ROUND 3 (combined, all three items at once) found 14 more and every one was fixed; audit_clean stays FALSE until a round comes back clean. Nothing new wrong with the removals themselves -- no orphaned data, props, types or CSS, and nothing still computed into nothing. Round 3's two observations here are both recorded rather than built: the lost card-level 'edited' flag is already decision EDITED-FLAG-2026-09-04 (REBUILD AS NEW UI, approved, in pending_kenneth), and the badge's departure from the schematic is now an open question below. What WAS missing was coverage: the rendered surface of the rework had none, so the header name the Barrier Race cross-refers to, the per-contract headline, and both directions of stopCostShown are now asserted. ROUND 5: no new defect in the removals themselves -- the auditor re-verified that isDirty/computeEditedRR/dirty/editedRR are gone with no orphans, that data.rrRatio/rrModel remain live via the context rail and tradeCardSnapshotOf, that firstPassage.invalidation still feeds BarrierRaceCard and data.exit.invalidation still hard-blocks send, and that stopCostShown gates the readout and its cross-reference from one expression. Rounds are counted together with the other two items. ROUND 6: no new defect in the removals themselves. But see the open question on discarded card edits -- deleting isDirty() removed the LAST reader of overlay.maxFill, overlay.invalidation and overlay.timeStopDays, so those are now pure orphaned state. The edits were already discarded by the send paths before this diff; the removals are what made it invisible.

decisions.q: SPEC DEVIATION raised by round 3: the schematic's card 03 puts the dollars-left ON the badge and per SHARE ('Caution - 71% of premium - $1.49 left'); what shipped kept the badge percent-only with per-CONTRACT dollars on the headline below. Which?
decisions.a: MATCH THE SCHEMATIC. The badge now reads '<pct>% of premium - $<x.xx>/share left'. Reason it matters beyond this card: the badge is what the ranking view will reuse, and there it would travel with only a percentage -- the half that does not say whether being wrong costs $8 or $800. Two consequences accepted deliberately: (1) the card now shows the same quantity twice in two units a foot apart (per share on the badge, per contract on the headline), so both strings name their unit; (2) '/share' rather than the schematic's bare '$1.49 left' because StatusBadge uppercases its label and is white-space:nowrap -- the CONTENT follows the schematic, the CASING follows the design system. AMENDED IN ROUND 6: the badge also leads with the VERDICT WORD ('CAUTION - 71% of premium - $1.49/share left'), which the schematic always had and round 5's first build dropped -- StatusBadge renders `label ?? STATUS_LABEL[status]`, so supplying a label REPLACES the word. Without it, two cards printing the same rounded percentage on opposite sides of the pass line differed only by colour. BUILT.

decisions.q: Round 6 verified that the card's edited Invalidation, Max fill and Time stop never reach a send path. Fix inside this branch, or record it and build later?
decisions.a: FIX NOW, INSIDE THIS BRANCH. Threaded the two fields that have consumers: Invalidation (becomes PortfolioPosition.stop, drives STOP_REACHED against the live underlying price) and Entry limit (posted as the broker order's limit_price on the quick Place Limit path and in AutoTradeArm, and shown in the button label). TradeCard's premiumStopTouchedRef generalised to a per-field TouchedFields map, so an untouched field caches null and keeps deferring to the live card value as mergePlan moves it -- the same rule piece 4 established for the premium stop. Max fill and Time stop NOT threaded: they have no consumer to thread them to, so it is a build, not a fix (see open questions).

decisions.q: The schematic (card 03) puts the dollars-left ON the badge and per SHARE ('Caution . 71% of premium . $1.49 left'). Shipped keeps the badge percent-only with per-CONTRACT dollars on the line beneath. Change it or keep it?
decisions.a: SUPERSEDED BY ITS OWN PREMISE BEING FALSE -- corrected in round 7, NOT by Kenneth; he needs to confirm or overrule this correction. The answer recorded here claimed 'Verified both are on screen: the badge prints the verdict word plus "N% OF PREMIUM"'. That verification was never true. formatStopLossBadge (lib/risk.ts) returns 'CAUTION - 71% of premium - $1.49/share left' -- the per-share dollars-left IS on the badge, so the premise ('shipped keeps the badge percent-only') described a code state that does not exist, and the follow-on note ('the per-share left is not printed') is false too. The question it re-asked had already been answered the other way by BADGE-SPEC-2026-09-05 ('MATCH THE SCHEMATIC ... BUILT'), which is what actually shipped and what round 6 then amended to lead with the verdict word. Two mutually exclusive decisions on one question, same date, and the later one edited the authoritative schematic to match a code state that never shipped. ACTION TAKEN IN ROUND 7: the schematic's card 03 has been put back to the badge the code produces and carries a CORRECTED note saying why; BADGE-SPEC-2026-09-05 stands as the live decision. No code changed -- the code was right throughout.

decisions.q: Card 03 heads the section 'Stop cost' and says every other line stays as it reads today; shipped reads 'MAX LOSS IF THE STOP IS HIT' (approved as NOTATION-2026-09-04 but never recorded as a departure). Amend the schematic, or revert the header?
decisions.a: AMEND THE SCHEMATIC. The shipped header stands.

decisions.q: Should a PREMIUM_STOP alert stamp the threshold it fired at, rather than the Alerts page resolving it live from the position (so editing a position silently relabels its historical alert rows with a threshold those alerts never used)?
decisions.a: YES -- the alert should show the threshold it actually fired at. APPROVED, NOT STARTED. Cross-cutting: a field on the toast, a persisted alertStore migration, and the same field from the backend generator's websocket path. Raised by round 5; the lossy Math.round on that label was already fixed there.

decisions.q: Thread the card's Max fill and Time stop through to a send path as well?
decisions.a: DEFERRED, confirmed by Kenneth. Neither has a consumer today, so it is a build (new persisted field, backend column, alert change), not the wiring fix Invalidation and Entry limit were. Stays an open question rather than being half-done inside an audit branch.

decisions.q: Round 7 finding 3: Max fill and Time stop render with the SAME click-to-edit affordance as the three fields that now reach the broker, but nothing anywhere consumes either one. Thread them, signal them, or leave them?
decisions.a: MADE READ-ONLY in round 7, pending Kenneth. Threading stays deferred (MAXFILL-TIMESTOP-2026-09-05 -- it is a build: a persisted field, a backend column and an alert change). But shipping two inert fields that look identical to three load-bearing ones was not part of that deferral, it was an omission: before this branch all five were inert and at least consistent. Both rows are now plain KV rows (the schematic draws them as plain fields, so this is not a spec deviation). REVERSIBLE in one line each if Kenneth would rather keep the affordance and add a marker instead.

decisions.q: Round 7 finding 4: the Invalidation field became PortfolioPosition.stop (compared against the live underlying by STOP_REACHED) while keeping min=0.01, no max and no directional check. Bound it?
decisions.a: BOUNDED, directionally, in round 7. Bullish: [50%, 99%] of the card's stock price. Bearish: [101%, 150%]. Clamps rather than rejects, matching the Premium stop field Round 5 bounded for the same reason. Deliberately WIDE -- it is there to reject a mistyped digit, not a wide stop. The two failures it closes on a $145 stock: '1400' fires a Critical STOP_REACHED (plus Gmail and Telegram) on the first 30s scan; '14' is worse because it is silent -- the send gate only requires a positive number, so the trade goes out believing it is protected by a level the underlying will never reach.

decisions.q: Round 7 finding 6: touchedRef was a one-way latch -- once a field was typed it was pinned for the life of Step 7 and mergePlan could no longer reach it. Round 6's own note calls 'a card with no way back to inheriting' the bad outcome. Add a way back?
decisions.a: YES -- clearing the input reverts the field to the plan's value and clears its touched flag, the same gesture the portfolio EditDrawer already uses to mean 'inherit the global'. Chosen over a revert button or a line of copy so it adds no control to a schematic-governed card and does not pre-empt EDITED-FLAG-2026-09-04, which is Kenneth's and still unbuilt. Surfaced only as an input tooltip, so it is undiscoverable until you hover -- the edited indicator is the right place to fix that properly.

decisions.q: Round 8 finding 2: an out-of-range entry in the card's three bounded fields was CLAMPED. On a $150 bullish card '1400' typed for '140' clamped to $148.50 -- 1% below spot -- stored as PortfolioPosition.stop, so STOP_REACHED fires Critical on the first intraday wiggle while the user believes the stop is 7% away. Clamp or reject?
decisions.a: REJECT, in round 8. Out of range now leaves the field's previous value on screen and reports nothing, which is the position the portfolio EditDrawer's premium-stop editor already took on the identical question ('showing the previous value back is the honest answer'). Two editors in one branch with opposite policies, and the card had the unsafe one on the field that becomes the position's stop. A clamp does not refuse a fat-finger, it renames it. Side benefit: this retires round 6's seed-outside-bounds hazard at the source -- the clamp was what made a bare focus-and-blur look like a deliberate edit when the SEED itself sat outside the bounds. REVERSES the clamp behaviour round 5 chose for the Premium stop field.

decisions.q: Round 8's CRITICAL: the Entry limit became the order's limit_price in this branch and was the only threaded field left unbounded (min=0.01, no max). Nothing else gates it -- checkTradeRisk and the capital-at-risk row both size off contractDetails.mid, and the backend's limit_price is an unvalidated Optional[float].
decisions.a: BOUNDED to [0.25x, 3x] of the live-or-scan mid. Of the three threaded fields this is the only one whose fat-finger is an EXECUTION error rather than an alerting one: on a $2.50 mid, '25.0' typed for '2.50' posted limit_price 25.0 on a BUY/OPEN order, and on a wide options book a marketable buy limit an order of magnitude above the ask is a real fill at a real price. Deliberately wider than the other two fields because paying up through the ask is a legitimate use of a limit order -- 3x catches the missing decimal point (10x) with room to spare.

decisions.q: Round 8 finding 3: the field bounds were anchored to data.price / contractDetails.mid, which come off scanResult -- and scanStore persists that to localStorage, so after a reload they can be days old.
decisions.a: ANCHORED ON THE LIVE QUOTE, falling back to the scan-time figures. The page already fetches both and renders them as 'Live stock:' and 'Live mid:' a few rows from the fields; they were simply never handed down. Without this, AAPL scanned at $145 and reopened at $200 rejected every sane stop below today's spot.

open_questions: Do the Q7 thresholds (0.80/0.70/0.60) hold on a real universe? Round 5 records them as taken as proposed, never measured.
Is Tradier's per-contract IV good enough in production to displace a solver for Phase A?

ivRank is conflated: market.py:1277 writes raw IV x100 into a field named for a percentile, 1291/1308 conditionally overwrite it with a genuine rank, and scan.py:610-616 broadcasts an ATM value across every strike. It is compared against iv_rank_pass_max: 34 and hard_reject.max_iv_rank: 70 -- a LIVE scoring/hard-reject defect, not a tidy-up.

Should the auto-trader's daily-loss gate size on the full premium instead of the premium stop? Since piece 4 the denominator can come from ArmRequest.premium_stop_pct, so a tighter declared stop shrinks premium_at_risk and lets more trades through -- and nothing enforces the declared stop, because the auto-trader places no protective order. Deliberately not clamped. ROUND 5 UPDATE: the reachability was far worse than this text implied -- the card's stop field was min=0.01 with no max, so one keystroke cut the denominator ~3000x via a field whose label says nothing about auto-trade sizing. That field is now bounded to 10-99% of the mid, so the remaining exposure is a deliberate 6x (a 10% stop against the 0.60 default), not a fat-finger. The underlying question -- full premium or declared stop -- stands.

Thread the card's Max fill and Time stop through to a send path? Deferred, and NOT a wiring fix: neither field has a consumer anywhere today. TIME_STOP fires on a hardcoded `dteRemaining <= 3` (alertEngine.ts:298) and PortfolioPosition carries no time-stop field at all; maxFill has no reader outside its own input. Threading either means a new persisted field, a backend column and an alert change -- a build. Invalidation and Entry limit, which DID have consumers, were threaded on 2026-09-05 (decision THREAD-EDITS-2026-09-05).

Round 7 finding 3, second half: the card prints 'Time stop 18d' (data.exit.timeStopDays) while the alert bearing that name fires on a hardcoded dteRemaining <= 3 (frontend/lib/alertEngine.ts). A trader reads an 18-day exit off the card and gets a 3-DTE one. Making the alert honour the card needs a persisted per-position field -- i.e. the deferred build -- so round 7 only removed the edit affordance. Relabel the row, build the field, or accept the disagreement?

Round 7 rejected finding 8 (the entry-limit/entryPrice denominator) on arithmetic: the threshold is entry x (1 - dollar/entry) = entry - dollar, so the dollar loss is preserved whatever entry price is stored. The residual is real but pre-existing and unrelated to the threading: for a LIMIT order the position's entry_price is the backend's save-time live quote, not the fill, so P&L and both stops are measured from a price the order may not have filled at. Worth its own decision?

Standing, unasked since the round 6 handoff: the loop has now caught regressions introduced by its own prior rounds three times (round 5's bounds re-opened round 4's stray click; the threading opened the round-trip defect; the round-trip fix's caches were left out of the scan-result clear). Does that change how many CLEAN rounds this branch needs before merging?

Round 8 finding 4 was a regression the round-7 clear-to-inherit gesture introduced: <input type='number'> sanitizes its value to '' for any half-typed literal ('132.', '.5'), which is the same string as a deliberate clear, so a user mid-keystroke had a committed edit thrown away (and in the portfolio EditDrawer, a live per-position stop PATCHed to null). Fixed by moving both inputs to type='text' inputMode='decimal'. Worth checking whether any OTHER number input in the app treats an empty value as a meaningful gesture.

traps: migrations/env.py:41 overwrites whatever sqlalchemy.url a caller sets with settings.DATABASE_URL. An alembic test that does not also set the env var silently migrates the real dev database. get_settings() is lru_cached, so clear the cache too.

A bs_iv test written against the reference contract (215C) alone passes and hides the entire defect.

Run the backend suite as plain `pytest`, with NO DATABASE_URL set. tests/conftest.py:54 does `os.environ.setdefault("DATABASE_URL", <isolated test db>)`, so it already isolates the run -- and because it is setdefault, an env var YOU export wins and defeats it. Exporting DATABASE_URL=sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory: (advice inherited from the alembic trap above, which applies only to alembic tests) makes tests/test_db_isolation.py fail: 1 failed / 1992 passed with it, all green without it. Round 5 chased that failure to ground -- do not read it as a real regression.

The backend venv is at backend/.venv, not backend/venv, and nothing outside it has pytest or pydantic. Round 5's audit subagent concluded 'pytest and pydantic are not installed in this container' and reported every backend finding as inspection-only. Both backend findings it raised that way turned out real, but tell an auditor the interpreter path (backend/.venv/bin/python) so it can verify rather than guess.
